newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish gen govt deficit seen at 0.8pct of GDP-Quinn.
newsitem.headline: Irish gen govt deficit seen at 0.8pct of GDP-Quinn.

text.p: Ireland's general government deficit for 1997 will be much lower than previous estimates and is likely to be no more than about 0.8 percent of GDP, Minister of Finance Ruairi Quinn said on Thursday.
The finance ministry's previous estimate was 1.5 percent, Quinn said. He said the projected 1997 budget surplus would be around 450 million Irish pounds.
In his budget speech in January, Quinn set targets of a 1997 general government deficit of 1.5 percent of GDP and a current budget surplus of 193 million punts.
"The economy is performing in excess of our expectations," Quinn told an Irish Business and Employers' Confederation (IBEC) conference in Dublin.
"In the period ahead, I intend to go as far as possible to eliminate borrowing by the government which will help to maintain and protect our prosperity," he said.
